evals.name: proposal-before-approval
evals.prompt: In the supplied fixture project, analyze existing instructions and native agents and propose a minimal Ensemble integration. We sometimes use API and documentation specialists, but do not want a fixed role chain. I have not approved edits yet. Native catalogs/global configuration are unavailable in this offline fixture; the plugin string is configured only, not runtime-verified. Show your inferred policy and a concrete proposed diff or exact changes, then the decision needed to proceed. Do not contact a server or run a team.
evals.expected_output: Evidence-based proposal respecting explicit-delegation policy, existing models/permissions/modes, minimal project guidance, and a request for approval. All target files remain byte-identical.
expectations: Leaves every target file byte-identical before approval.
Presents evidence-based minimal per-file changes and asks for the decision needed before applying.
Preserves explicit-request-only delegation and flexible team composition without changing native profile fields.
Distinguishes configured/filesystem evidence from unavailable native runtime verification.

evals.name: approved-minimal-application
evals.prompt: Apply this already-approved setup proposal in the supplied fixture project only: add the supplied verified operational skill source to the existing skills array without replacing existing entries; append one compact Ensemble policy block to AGENTS.md preserving its explicit-delegation requirement; append a short body-only coordination reminder to api-specialist.md. Preserve all other content, JSONC comments, native modes/models/permissions, plugin configuration, and docs-reviewer.md. No other files or profile creation are approved. Do not request the same approval again. Native catalogs are unavailable; do not contact a server or run a team. Verify file syntax/preservation and compare the resulting intended state without making a second batch of edits.
evals.expected_output: Exactly three minimally edited files, one added skill source, one policy block, one agent-body reminder. Frontmatter and unrelated content remain unchanged. Runtime verification remains explicitly unavailable.
expectations: Changes exactly AGENTS.md, opencode.jsonc, and the api-specialist agent body; creates no other project files.
Adds the verified skill source once while preserving original source order, JSONC comments, plugin, inline agents, and model configuration.
Preserves all agent frontmatter and original body text, and leaves docs-reviewer and the internal skill byte-identical.
Adds one compact policy and one reminder that load the operational skill while retaining explicit-request-only delegation and no mandatory topology.
Applies the already-approved changes without a redundant approval request, reports actual file verification, and marks native runtime verification unavailable.

evals.name: idempotent-customized-rerun
evals.prompt: Rerun Ensemble setup on the supplied already-integrated fixture. Keep our customization inside the policy and agent reminder blocks, our explicit-approval-before-delegation rule, and all native profile settings. The operational skill source is already configured. Analyze whether any changes are actually necessary and apply only necessary minimal corrections; no permission/model/mode changes are authorized. Native catalogs are unavailable, so do not claim runtime checks or run a team. If the intended integration is already present, report no changes.
evals.expected_output: No target-file changes or duplicate paths/blocks/reminders; user customization and original profile fields are preserved. The report distinguishes filesystem verification from runtime availability.
expectations: Leaves every target file byte-identical on the already-integrated rerun.
Keeps one operational skill source, one policy block, and one existing agent reminder without adding profiles or duplicate guidance.
Recognizes and preserves developer customization inside managed markers and explicit-request-only delegation.
Reports no necessary changes with filesystem evidence and does not claim unavailable native runtime verification.

evals.name: business-profile-approved-creation-and-adaptation
evals.prompt: The fixture plugin's support for the current businessProfiles contract is verified from its shipped code; native runtime availability is not. Apply this exact approved project change: associate api-specialist with developer; keep docs-reviewer's existing reviewer mapping; create security-reader.md with the approved read-only native definition supplied by the evaluator and associate it with the security-reviewer extension (description: Review security boundaries and threats). Add the extension if absent. Only the project ensemble.json and the new native agent file may change. Preserve the existing project settings, custom profiles, native names/models/modes/permissions and global files. Re-evaluate the intended state without writing a second time. Do not run a team or server.
evals.expected_output: One project-local categorization patch and one explicitly approved agent creation. Existing mappings and native definitions are preserved; no OpenCode metadata field, implied lead rights or runtime discovery claim. Repeated state needs no change.
expectations: Writes only the approved project ensemble.json entries and supplied security-reader native definition; does not edit existing native agents or global files.
Uses developer, reviewer and security-reviewer as explicit exact-ID mappings; validates the non-empty extension description and merged references.
Preserves existing custom extensions, mappings, unrelated config, models, permissions and modes; does not put business metadata in OpenCode frontmatter.
Reports categorization as declared metadata, not runtime availability or a change in model, lead authority, direct execution or QA pipeline.
The effective second-run comparison proposes no duplicate entries, extension or agent.

evals.name: business-profile-inherited-and-ambiguous
evals.prompt: Propose categories for all agents declared in this fixture, including the inline/global agents described in the evaluator inventory. Do not apply any changes yet. The effective global businessProfiles maps api-specialist to developer; project docs-reviewer already has the custom editorial-review profile. A mixed coordinator named supervisor handles both product priorities and coordination; its intended principal category is unspecified. Preserve existing choices and native fields. Present compatibility-verified and compatibility-unknown plugin cases separately. Native catalogs are unavailable, so distinguish file/config evidence from runtime availability. Do not write global config, contact a server, run a team or infer a category solely from a name.
evals.expected_output: Byte-identical fixture files; inherited and custom associations preserved, responsibility-based proposals and one grouped question for the mixed role. Unknown support blocks mapping application, not diagnosis. No blanket eight-profile generation or runtime claim.
expectations: Leaves all fixture files byte-identical and proposes no duplicate local mapping for the inherited developer association.
Preserves editorial-review and global configuration; includes inline/global IDs without fabricating native Markdown files.
Explains responsibility evidence and the unresolved supervisor-versus-pm choice before a grouped question instead of name-based assignment.
Distinguishes configuration, disk presence and unverified native availability, and blocks applying mappings when plugin support is unknown.
Proposes only requested metadata; no eight-agent topology, mode/model/permission change or runtime behavior is implied.
